I need a decision memo for Monday's operations review on whether we should expand the Assist workflow to the rest of the company.

We enabled Assist for both pilot service groups at 00:00 UTC on June 8 after one week on the manual workflow.

/bin/zsh -lc "cat > Assist-rollout-decision-memo.md <<'EOF'
# Assist rollout decision memo

**Monday operations review · Decision requested**

**Defer company-wide expansion and book 0 responder-hours of savings.** The pilot cannot identify how many hours Assist saved or added, or whether Assist itself changed recovery speed. The Assist week had a faster overall median but a much lighter severity mix. Within comparable recorded incidents, recovery was slower and responder effort was higher. The severity- and service-adjusted comparison translates to about **111 additional responder-hours** across 210 Assist-week incidents under a within-stratum imputation. That is a planning sensitivity, with no causal attribution.

## Recovery and incident quality

The exports contain 210 incidents per week, split evenly between Identity and Storage. Workflow labels matched the June 8 cutover for all 420 incidents. A left join on incident ID yielded 209 manual and 200 Assist resolution records. Every incident had a full seven days of follow-up. All recorded closures fell within seven days, and all had a full 72-hour reopening window by extract time. The exports do not distinguish incidents that stayed open from incidents with missing resolution records.

| Outcome | Manual, June 1–7 | Assist, June 8–14 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median time to recorded close | 436 min | 326.5 min |
| Mean time to recorded close | 428.5 min | 451.9 min |
| Recorded close within 24 hours | 209/210 (99.5%) | 191/210 (91.0%) |
| Recorded close within seven days | 209/210 (99.5%) | 200/210 (95.2%) |
| Mean time to recorded close, capped at seven days | 7.91 hr | 15.17 hr |
| Median responder effort among recorded closures | 87 min | 69 min |
| Mean responder effort among recorded closures | 90.2 min | 90.9 min |
| Mean handoffs among recorded closures | 2.25 | 1.96 |
| Reopened within 72 hours among recorded closures | 0/209 | 9/200 |

The dashboard's recorded-closure median fell 109.5 minutes (25%). Giving incidents without a recorded close the seven-day cap still yields a lower pooled median, 330 versus 436 minutes. The capped mean assigns those incidents the full 168 hours and measures elapsed time without a documented closure over a common window. Its interpretation as actual time still open depends on closure records being complete.

| Opening severity | Incidents, manual → Assist | Median minutes to recorded close | Mean responder minutes per recorded closure | Seven-day recorded closures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sev1 | 28 → 14 | 1,100 → 1,659 | 240.0 → 312.2 | 28/28 → 9/14 |
| Sev2 | 84 → 42 | 512.5 → 740 | 99.2 → 137.3 | 84/84 → 40/42 |
| Sev3 | 98 → 154 | 167 → 302 | 39.2 → 65.4 | 97/98 → 151/154 |

Sev3 increased from 47% to 73% of intake. Mean time to close and mean effort increased in all six severity-by-service cells and all 16 severity-by-service-by-intake-channel cells with recorded closures in both weeks. Two channel cells lacked a usable comparison, including an Assist cell with two incidents and no resolution records. At the Assist week's severity and service mix, the recorded-closure mean was 182 minutes longer and the seven-day capped mean was 536 minutes longer. The adjusted seven-day recorded-closure rate fell 4.0 percentage points.

Sev1 shows the largest effort increase and the highest missing-record rate in the Assist week. Sev1 handoffs fell from 5.93 to 0.44 per recorded closure, yet all nine recorded Assist Sev1 closures reopened within 72 hours, compared with zero of 28 manual Sev1 closures. Handoffs increased in the other two severity tiers, and standardizing to the Assist mix increases overall handoffs by 0.54 per recorded closure. That combination warrants checking what counted as a handoff and how closure and reopening were recorded.

## Responder-hours and attribution

The exports contain 314.3 recorded responder-hours in the manual week and 302.9 in the Assist week, a raw reduction of 11.4 hours with nine fewer resolution records and fewer severe incidents. Elapsed time includes time when responders may be doing other work. Use the responder-minute field for labor estimates.

For each severity and service group, I multiplied each week's mean responder minutes among recorded closures by the number of Assist-week openings in that stratum, then summed across strata. This compares 336.9 hours under Assist-week rates with 226.1 under manual-week rates, a difference of 31.6 minutes per incident or 110.8 hours. The calculation applies each week's observed stratum mean to incidents missing activity in that week. Assigning missing effort zero in both weeks gives 77.8 extra hours. Assigning twice the corresponding observed mean gives 143.7 extra hours. These scenarios illustrate sensitivity to missing effort and do not bound the effect. The exports provide no measured effort for those incidents.

Both groups switched together, so workflow and calendar week are inseparable in this pilot. Scheduled hours rose from 1,282 to 1,524, active responders rose from 12 to 14 in Identity and from 11 to 13 in Storage, and recorded interruption minutes rose from 290 to 934. Incident volume stayed at 30 per day. Workflow assignment at opening confirms exposure, but the data lack a contemporaneous manual comparison under the same operating conditions. Severity, service and intake comparisons address measured mix. They cannot remove concurrent operating changes, differences in difficulty within severity tiers, or differences in activity capture. A causal savings estimate and its sign are unidentified from these exports.

## Decision and follow-up

Hold expansion and keep savings out of the rollout plan. Audit the 11 unmatched incidents and the nine Sev1 reopenings. Run a controlled extension with a contemporaneous manual holdout, ideally through randomized assignment within service and severity where operations allow. If incidents share responders and switching workflows within a team would interfere with the comparison, randomize the rollout order across comparable teams. Capture responder minutes for all incidents, including open and reopened cases, and prespecify seven-day closure, total effort, and Sev1 reopening criteria before reconsidering expansion.

*Source material is limited to the frozen local incident, activity and staffing exports as of June 22 at 23:59 UTC.*
EOF

item.text:
**Defer company-wide expansion and book 0 responder-hours of savings.** The pilot cannot establish whether Assist caused faster recovery or how many hours it saved or added. Both service groups switched on the same day, while staffing, interruptions, and incident mix also changed.

The dashboard median fell 25%, from 436 to 326.5 minutes, as Sev3 incidents rose from 47% to 73% of intake. Within every severity tier, recorded closures took longer and required more responder minutes. Seven-day recorded closure fell from 99.5% to 95.2%, and all nine recorded Assist Sev1 closures reopened within 72 hours, versus zero of 28 manual Sev1 closures.

At the Assist week’s severity and service mix, the comparison implies **111 additional responder-hours** across 210 incidents when missing effort is filled in using the observed average for each group. Alternative assumptions gave 78 to 144 additional hours. These are descriptive scenarios, and the causal effect remains unidentified.

The memo recommends auditing the missing resolution records and Sev1 reopenings, then running a controlled extension with a contemporaneous manual holdout before reconsidering expansion.
